Validate the following vignette.

Patient demographics:
  age: 68
  gender: Female
  ethnicity: African
  relationship_status: Married
  occupation: Unemployed
  trauma_type: Physical abuse by romantic partner
  pcl5: 41

Patient-reported symptoms:
  Triggers: Sleeping Alone: Sleeping alone or in an unfamiliar place, Feeling Vulnerable: Feeling emotionally vulnerable, Olfactory (Earth/Outdoor): Soil or outdoor smells
  Maladaptive Strategies: People Pleasing: go along with whatever others want to feel safe, Busyness: I work hard at keeping busy with other things, Mental Distraction: keep mind occupied all the time
  Threat: Safe Zone Only: I only feel safe in a very limited number of places, Sleep Vigilance: I have difficulty falling asleep because I need to stay alert, Alert at Home: I feel on guard even inside my own home
  Memory: Uncontrolled Access: The memory forces its way into my mind when I do not want it to, Blocked Before Complete: I find myself pushing the memory away before I can fully recall it, Triggered Without Warning: Something in my surroundings can instantly bring back the full memory without warning

Vignette:
Akua had always thought of her marriage to Kwame as a sanctuary, a place where she could be herself without fear of judgment. But that all changed one fateful night 20 years ago, when Kwame's anger boiled over and he turned on her. The memory of the physical abuse still lingered, refusing to be fully recalled yet never truly forgotten. Akua remembered the feeling of being trapped in their small bedroom, the scent of damp earth from the potted plants on the windowsill mingling with the metallic tang of fear. She had pushed Kwame away, but not before he had left his mark - a bruise that would take weeks to heal, and a wound that would never fully close. In the years since, Akua had developed a keen sense of threat awareness, always on the lookout for potential dangers. Even in her own home, she felt on guard, as if waiting for the other shoe to drop. At night, she found herself lying awake, vigilant for any sign of movement or sound that might signal Kwame's return. Sleep became a luxury she could ill afford. When Kwame passed away five years ago, Akua thought she would finally be able to rest easy. But instead, she found herself struggling with the uncertainty of being alone at night. The silence was oppressive, and the darkness seemed to press in on her from all sides. She began to dread sleeping alone, feeling vulnerable and exposed. Akua's way of coping was to fill every waking moment with activity - cleaning, cooking, gardening - anything to keep her mind occupied and distract herself from the memories that lurked just beneath the surface. She also found herself people-pleasing, going along with whatever others wanted in order to feel safe and accepted. Despite these efforts, the memories still managed to break through. A whiff of damp earth or outdoor smells would transport Akua back to that terrible night, and she would find herself reliving the fear and helplessness all over again. Sometimes, it happened without warning - a sight, a sound, a smell - and Akua would be right back in that bedroom, fighting for her life. Akua's world began to shrink as she avoided more and more situations that might trigger these memories. She stopped going out with friends, afraid of being caught off guard by some unexpected stimulus. Her relationships with her children and grandchildren suffered as a result, as they struggled to understand why Akua was no longer the warm and nurturing presence she once had been. Lately, Akua's sleep vigilance had begun to take its toll on her physical health. She felt exhausted all the time, and the constant stress was starting to affect her relationships with those closest to her. It was then that Akua realized she needed help - not just to manage her symptoms, but to reclaim her life. As she sat in her small living room, surrounded by the familiar comforts of home, Akua felt a glimmer of hope. Maybe, just maybe, she could learn to feel safe again - not just in this one place, but out in the world beyond. The thought was both exhilarating and terrifying, but for the first time in years, Akua felt willing to take that risk.
